findings.message: A different agent (Claude) checked the work in a separate headless process.

Most rows map correctly to exact test names, and the fallback mapping now covers both declaration orders. Two problems block approval. First, the route-admission row for "a different exact model" points to an assertion that cannot catch the failure it claims to cover. Second, the map replaces the per-block limits from the proof map with one generic sentence. That lets several rows claim more than their tests prove, most visibly the termination row's "headless" and "readable" claims. Smaller gaps are listed as warnings.

Route-admission row 1 (case c1dc4b6f…, 'complete passing admission evidence with a different exact model → the requested explicit route is absent') is mapped only to 'admits exact models and explicit runtime defaults without conflating them'. In that test, codex evidence is a runtime default with no model, so the excluded codex/gpt-5.6-sol route is never compared against a different exact model. Nor is the excluded claude-default route, because there the evidence is exact and the route is a default. A faulty filter that admits any route when both the route and the evidence carry a model, matching on reviewer alone, would still pass every mapped assertion. The test that actually exercises this row is 'preserves admitted degraded labeling and deterministically exhausts an empty set': evidence codex/gpt-6-astra against route codex/gpt-5.6-sol gives []. It is not mapped. The source_limit claim that 'one exact assertion tests both matched and unmatched explicit routes' therefore overstates the proof. The proof map's certification gap requires wrong identity to be distinguished as its own outcome.

Every case uses the same generic source_limit ('Execution only… No live reviewer qualification or host lifecycle claim'). This drops the per-block limits that proof-map.md says certification must keep: 'Minimal stored bytes are not eligible qualification evidence', 'Inline fixture ordering, not production harness pre-egress proof', 'Reader discrimination; actual oracle replay is separate', 'Synthetic mechanics; failed Codex 38/63 stays unqualified', 'Exact selectors/defaults; no alias qualification inferred', 'Controlled reviewer; no native-host enrollment claim' and 'Text contract; no NTB comprehension proof'. Concrete consequence for the termination case (252a72f4…): it claims 'checkpointed paired headless results' and that the 'paired raw observation remain[s] readable'. But the test writes outputs with no dispatch_mode or confirmed_model and metadata with no reviewer or requested_model, then reads only raw JSON, never through readExecutionCheckpoint. A writer that dropped the headless or confirmation fields would pass, and the map would still report the headless and readability clauses as covered. Each block's accepted limit needs to be restored.

Fallback row 1 (56a38005…, 'actually fails with an eligible typed failure') is mapped to the codexFails=true cases. Those cases make the codex stub exit 7 and assert only that both markers exist and that REVIEW_INDEPENDENCE_REDUCED appears. Nothing asserts the typed failure recorded for the codex route in review_routes. The ordering claim is reasonably supported, because a fallback-first route would never invoke codex, but the 'typed' part of the clause is not. Either narrow the claim or mark the clause as unsupported.

Installed-rule row 1 (89c0627f…) claims the review 'succeeds with unchanged Implementation bytes'. The mapped test asserts only exit status 0 for the repeated review; it never compares Implementation bytes. Under the proof map's guidance this should be an explicit unsupported clause, not an implied pass.

Retained-reuse rows (5d3ebf9d… through 773571…) treat 'before any reviewer launch' as proven. The 'launch' is a marker file written by an inline bun --eval script, not the production harness. The proof map records this exact limit; without it, the rows read as pre-egress proof.

All mapped full_name values match the visible test titles once parameters are expanded (it.each $label / %s substitutions and describe prefixes). The fallback-order block covers both declaration orders and both the success and failure branches, as the proof map's certification gap requires.
